correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the greedy-suffix recurrence \(E_j\)=\(E_{j+1}\)+\(O_j\) and \(O_j\)=\(O_{j+1}\) (equal) or \(E_{j+2}\) (unequal), with E_{m+1}=2 and (E_m,O_m)=(3,1). Every change from an equal to unequal orientation boundary strictly increases \(E_1\). A single equal boundary after j causes the exact loss \(F_jF_{m-j}\); Fibonacci addition gives minimum \(F_{m-2}\) uniquely at j=2 or m-2 for \(m\ge 5\). Every lower-universality word has at most \(F_{m+2}\), below the runner-up. Independent greedy-suffix DP and block recurrences checked all orientation words for m=2..11; exact global exhaustive enumeration checked all binary words of lengths 10,12,14,16,18. Direct subsequence enumeration checked tiny instances. All passed. The proof, not the finite experiments, establishes universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of the close 2026 Fibonacci-extremal proof establishes only the maximum \(F_{m+3}\), and does not state the second value, the gap \(F_{m-2}\), or the exact four runner-up words. The 2021 primary paper develops fixed-index extremality but not a strict second optimum. The 2022 nearly-universal paper gives a count recursion without an all-length stability optimization. An explicit defect-product calculation and exact near-equality analysis are nontrivial further conclusions. Residual historical synonym and unseen-source risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The sharp first gap and full four-word equality class quantify stability of a natural known Fibonacci maximum in subsequence omission. They give an exact all-parameter obstruction to any near-optimal absent-count target, and a structural diagnosis of where the first costly departure from alternating arches can occur. This is not a routine substitution into the known maximum: strict repair monotonicity, defect transfer and the Fibonacci product minimization are necessary.
